name: Alternanthera

project_scope.selection_mode: Master Plant Pool rows 39–41, three installed canonical species
project_scope.range_policy: Preserve existing non-native comparison classifications in species records; no range audit or new status assigned.

look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: find an OPPOSITE leaf pair, then follow its node to the flower cluster. Is the whitish papery head round and on a distinct stalk (A. philoxeroides), or small and crowded near a prostrate stem (A. caracasana / A. pungens)? With a hand lens, compare the flower bracts: distinctly sharp prickly tips favor A. pungens. Check several flowering nodes; wet versus dry habitat alone does not prove identity.
shared_genus_traits: Mostly opposite simple leaves and small, densely packed flowers with persistent papery tepals/bracts; what looks like a white flower ball consists of many small flowers.
Stems may sprawl or root at nodes; branching habit alone varies with water and disturbance.
Tiny flowers and one-seeded fruits need close magnification; bract texture, cluster stalk and node architecture are more useful than leaf greenness.

species_comparison_matrix.caracasana: Low prostrate mat, often disturbed ground
species_comparison_matrix.philoxeroides: Sprawling perennial, wet banks or floating mats; can root at nodes
species_comparison_matrix.pungens: Creeping ground mat, often dry/disturbed sites
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Photograph entire attached stem and root nodes; habitat supports but never proves ID.

species_comparison_matrix.caracasana: Compact whitish papery clusters, often near stems
species_comparison_matrix.pungens: Small dense heads near creeping stems
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Side view with peduncle fully visible and scale; examine multiple nodes.

species_comparison_matrix.philoxeroides: White papery floral parts, not the conspicuously prickly khakiweed head
species_comparison_matrix.pungens: Sharp straw-colored prickly bracts are a high-value clue
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Same magnification flower-head dissection; do not rely on overall color.

species_comparison_matrix.philoxeroides: Opposite leaves; creeping stems may root at nodes
species_comparison_matrix.pungens: Opposite often rounded/obovate leaves on prostrate stems
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Attached mid-stem leaf pair, shape and rooting node with ruler.

species_comparison_matrix.caracasana: Tiny fruit enclosed by persistent papery parts
species_comparison_matrix.philoxeroides: Small flower parts in round heads; fruit macro not yet documented
species_comparison_matrix.pungens: Mature fruit and bract-tip macro still needed
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Dissect mature heads; refer ambiguous microscopic characters to taxonomy review.

look_here_first: Find an attached opposite leaf pair and inspect its node.
Trace flower heads to their stalks: distinctly pedunculate globes versus compact near-stem clusters.
Magnify bract tips; identify sharply prickly straw-colored bracts versus softer papery scales.
Photograph the full plant and habitat as supporting evidence; collect mature fruit when uncertain.
overlap_cautions: A. caracasana and A. pungens both make low disturbed-ground mats with small papery heads; a flower-head bract macro is essential.
A. philoxeroides can grow terrestrially, so wetland/floating habitat is not an exclusive key.
Leaf shape and color overlap and vary with conditions; avoid species identification from foliage alone.
Existing source-pool comparison/non-native metadata belongs to species records and is not altered by this lesson.

comparison_cards.title: Mat chaff-flower vs khakiweed
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Both creep along the ground; inspect sharp straw-colored bract tips in A. pungens against A. caracasana.
photo_requirements: same-scale flower head and bract-tip macros

comparison_cards.title: Alligatorweed vs terrestrial chaff-flowers
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Distinct stalked round white flower heads on A. philoxeroides; confirm attached leaf nodes and bract details.
photo_requirements: opposite leaf pairs and rooting nodes

confusable_genera.name: Gomphrena
confusable_genera.caution: Can also have papery globular flower heads; compare attached leaf arrangement and dissected floral bracts rather than head color alone.

confusable_genera.name: Amaranthus
confusable_genera.caution: Usually has a different clustered spike/glomerule architecture and often alternate leaves; inspect nodes and individual flower bracts.
